xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-3537: Command Deck: per-project live CI chip — latest main run status + link, webhook-fed

plan.title: Command Deck: per-project live CI chip — latest main run status + link, webhook-fed
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5

metadata.sizeJustification: 24 files, under the 25-file limit. The subsystem count reads 7 only because the first-two-path-segments heuristic counts two individual documentation files — docs/EXTERNAL-EVENT-STREAM.md and CLAUDE.md — as separate subsystems. The real breadth is six: contracts, src/lib, dashboard server, dashboard frontend, tests, docs. The work is one vertical slice that cannot ship in halves: a server-side CI record with no chip renders nothing for the operator, and a chip with no record has nothing to render, so splitting into sibling issues would ship a partial feature in violation of the deliver-complete-features rule. The eight items are already decomposed to one focused change each and are independently reviewable.

narratives.Problem: The Command Deck never says whether a project's default branch is green, so the operator leaves the dashboard for GitHub to find out. Overdeck already receives check_suite webhooks for every tracked repo but discards the ones that matter: src/lib/webhook-handlers.ts:319 returns early when check_suite.pull_requests is empty, which is exactly the shape of a push to main.
narratives.Proposal: Stop dropping default-branch check_suite events. Map the event's repository to a registered project, emit one new domain event (project.ci_suite_observed) per GitHub Actions suite, and let a shared reducer aggregate those observations into a per-project record inside the existing read model (ReadModelState.ciByProjectKey). A boot-time REST fill via gh api emits the same event shape so the record is correct before the first webhook, and a 15-minute refill repairs dropped deliveries. The frontend reads the record with a Zustand selector and renders a compact chip in the project header linking to that commit's checks on GitHub. No new store, no frontend polling, no new WebSocket channel. Full verified design in .pan/drafts/PAN-3537.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Feature-branch or PR CI state — default branch only; per-PR CI is surfaced elsewhere.
- Changing the GitHub App's event subscription or permissions (explicitly forbidden by the issue).
- Per-job check_run granularity in the chip; suite-level completed/total is the live feed.
- A CI panel, run history, or run list anywhere else (God View, Stage, release panel). The chip is the only new surface.
- Any durable persistence of CI state — the record is disposable cache rebuilt from REST on every boot.
- Any frontend polling loop, refetch interval, or new WebSocket channel.
- Re-running or cancelling workflows from the dashboard.
- GitLab CI. Only projects with github_repo get a chip.

autoDecisions.summary: The REST fill uses `gh api`, not src/lib/github-app.ts
autoDecisions.rationale: Verified live: the overdeck-agent App's permissions are checks/contents/metadata/pull_requests/statuses — there is no `actions` scope, so an installation token 403s on GET /repos/{repo}/actions/runs. `gh api` is the operator-token mechanism src/lib/overdeck/project-pipelines.ts:99-106 already uses for the release panel, and it was verified returning 200 for repos/eltmon/overdeck/actions/runs?branch=main.

autoDecisions.summary: Only check suites whose app.slug is `github-actions` feed the record
autoDecisions.rationale: A real main commit (7fe22a07 on eltmon/overdeck) has 7 check suites; 4 belong to vercel, mintlify, github-pages and posthog and sit in `queued` indefinitely. Aggregating them would pin the chip at 'in progress' forever. Mirrors the advisory-filter precedent in src/lib/advisory-checks.ts.

autoDecisions.summary: The record is keyed by head SHA and aggregates every Actions suite for that SHA
autoDecisions.rationale: One push to main produced two workflow runs with distinct check_suite_ids (no-planning-on-main success, CI in_progress). Picking whichever run the API returns first would let a trivial guard workflow paint the chip green while CI is failing.

autoDecisions.summary: One event type (project.ci_suite_observed) serves both the webhook and the REST fill
autoDecisions.rationale: Both express the same fact — a suite was observed in a state at a time — so one reducer case and one staleness rule cover both. Two event types would mean two merge policies that must be kept consistent by hand.

autoDecisions.summary: When the head SHA changes, the newer observedAt wins and resets the suite set
autoDecisions.rationale: Commit ordering is not derivable from a check_suite payload, and resolving it would cost an extra API call per event. Observation recency is the only tiebreak available in-payload, and it is what a live status chip actually wants.
A known-red workflow should read red the moment it is known, not after unrelated workflows finish settling.

Style guide v1.2 colour restraint caps a data-dense row at one colored signal, and a permanently green chip on every project row all day is decoration rather than signal. Colour is reserved for in_progress (--info, machine working) and failure (--destructive, broken).

autoDecisions.summary: The chip is absent when the read model holds no record for the project key
autoDecisions.rationale: Satisfies the issue's 'no dead chrome' requirement without plumbing extra project config to the frontend: the fill only creates records for projects whose repo it can actually read.

autoDecisions.summary: A 15-minute server-side refill supplements the boot fill
autoDecisions.rationale: Webhooks arrive over a smee relay and can be dropped; with a boot-only fill a long-running dashboard would show stale CI indefinitely. The refill is server-side, so the issue's no-frontend-polling requirement is untouched.

autoDecisions.summary: The new event is promoted to the public external-stream catalog
autoDecisions.rationale: 'Is main green' is exactly the signal a third-party sidecar wants, and docs/EXTERNAL-EVENT-STREAM.md requires the promoting PR to add the catalog row in the same change.

items.title: Add the project.ci_suite_observed event, ProjectCiSnapshot state, and deriveProjectCi helper to contracts

expected_outputs: tests/dashboard/event-reducers.test.ts passes including the new project.ci_suite_observed cases

narrative.Action: Follow PRD section 6.1-6.5. Add ProjectCiSuiteObservedEvent to packages/contracts/src/events.ts (next to BeadsFreshnessChangedEvent at line 38) with the JSDoc block given in PRD 6.1, and register it in the DomainEvent union at line 1349. Add ProjectCiSuite and ProjectCiSnapshot schemas to packages/contracts/src/types.ts before DashboardSnapshot (line 525), and add the optional ciByProjectKey field to DashboardSnapshot. In packages/contracts/src/event-reducers.ts add ciByProjectKey to ReadModelState (after embedProgressBySessionId), to INITIAL_READ_MODEL_STATE, to syncSnapshot, and add the applyEvent case exactly as written in PRD 6.3 (create / same-SHA merge / newer-SHA replace / older-SHA drop). Create packages/contracts/src/project-ci.ts exporting ProjectCiState, DerivedProjectCi and deriveProjectCi per PRD 6.4, re-exported from index.ts. Finally add `ciByProjectKey: state.ciByProjectKey` to buildSnapshot() in src/dashboard/server/read-model.ts (line 410-447) so a fresh page load carries the record. Failure outranks in_progress in the derivation; the failed-conclusion set mirrors FAILING_CHECK_CONCLUSIONS at src/lib/webhook-handlers.ts:196.

Emit a CI observation from default-branch check_suite webhooks

expected_outputs: both named test files pass, including the five null cases and the merge-gate-untouched case

narrative.Action: Follow PRD section 6.7. Create src/lib/ci/project-ci-observation.ts exporting the pure resolveProjectForRepo(fullName, projects) and observationFromCheckSuite(payload, now, projects) functions; both take the project list as an injectable parameter defaulting to listProjectsSync() (src/lib/projects.ts:546) so tests need no config on disk. The default branch is config.workspace?.default_branch ?? 'main' (src/lib/projects.ts:54). observationFromCheckSuite returns null for: unregistered repo, missing check_suite, app.slug other than 'github-actions', head_branch other than the project default branch, and missing head_sha or id. Then in src/lib/webhook-handlers.ts extend the check_suite member of WebhookPayload (line 32-36) with id, head_branch, head_sha and app.slug, and insert the observation emit at the top of handleCheckSuitePromise (line 315) BEFORE the existing isTrackedRepositorySync and pull_requests guards — the project registry, not the App tracked-repo allowlist, decides project mapping. Emit via appendDomainEventAsync from the emit-door item. Leave every existing merge-gate line below untouched.

Add the gh-api REST fill that seeds CI observations per project

expected_outputs: src/lib/overdeck/__tests__/project-ci-fill.test.ts passes with a stubbed ghApi and no network access

narrative.Action: Follow PRD section 6.8. Create src/lib/overdeck/project-ci-fill.ts modelled on src/lib/overdeck/project-pipelines.ts — same promisify(execFile) shape (line 29) and the same injectable GhApi type (line 97-106), never execSync. Export fillProjectCiObservations(project, deps) which returns [] when github_repo is unset, calls repos/<repo>/actions/runs?branch=<default>&per_page=20, takes workflow_runs[0].head_sha as the current SHA, keeps only runs with that head_sha, and maps each to an observation with suiteId String(run.check_suite_id), status run.status, conclusion run.conclusion, htmlUrl run.html_url and observedAt run.updated_at. Using run.updated_at rather than wall-clock is deliberate: it makes a fill lose to a fresher webhook under the reducer's staleness rule instead of stomping it. Also export fillAllProjectCi(deps) which iterates listProjectsSync() projects with a github_repo, appends every observation through the injectable append (defaulting to appendDomainEventAsync), and returns the count appended. Any gh failure yields [] for that project so the chip simply does not render.

items.title: Given a stubbed ghApi returning three runs — two sharing the newest head_sha and one older — When fillProjectCiObservations runs, Then it returns exactly two observations, each carrying the run's html_url and stringified check_suite_id
Given a stubbed ghApi that rejects, When fillProjectCiObservations runs, Then it returns an empty array and throws nothing
Given a project whose config has no github_repo, When fillProjectCiObservations runs, Then it returns an empty array without calling ghApi
Given two projects with github_repo and a stubbed append, When fillAllProjectCi runs, Then append receives one project.ci_suite_observed event per kept run and the returned count equals that number
Run the CI fill at dashboard boot and repair it every 15 minutes

expected_outputs: the refill interval test passes using vi.useFakeTimers and vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync

narrative.Action: Follow PRD section 6.9. In src/dashboard/server/main.ts, immediately after the existing `void reconcileStaleGitHubBlockers()` block at line 747, call fillAllProjectCi() with a catch that warns, then schedule a 15-minute setInterval that calls it again and .unref()s the timer so it never holds the process open. Export the interval scheduling as a small named function from src/lib/overdeck/project-ci-fill.ts (for example startProjectCiRefill(intervalMs, deps)) so it can be tested without booting the server. The interval test MUST use vi.useFakeTimers() plus vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(15 * 60 * 1000) — a real wall-clock wait is banned by the repo's fake-timer rule. This is a dashboard boot-path change: it must be runtime-boot-tested against a throwaway instance, never hot-patched onto the live server.

items.title: Given fake timers and a stubbed fill, When startProjectCiRefill is called and timers advance 15 minutes, Then the fill has been invoked a second time
Given a fill that rejects, When the boot call and a scheduled tick both run, Then neither rejection propagates and the interval continues firing
Given the scheduled interval, When it is created, Then unref() is applied so the timer does not keep the Node process alive
Add the ProjectCiChip component, store selector, and chip styles

expected_outputs: ProjectCiChip.test.tsx passes for the absent, queued, in_progress, success and failure states

narrative.Action: Follow PRD section 6.10. Add selectProjectCi(projectKey) to src/dashboard/frontend/src/lib/store.ts next to selectScanProgress (line 624). Create ProjectCiChip.tsx exactly as sketched in the PRD: it returns null when no record exists, calls deriveProjectCi from @overdeck/contracts, renders a <span role="link" tabIndex={0} data-testid="project-ci-chip" data-ci-state={state}> with label 'CI' for success, 'CI ✗' for failure and 'CI <completed>/<total>' otherwise, and opens the derived href with window.open(href, '_blank', 'noopener,noreferrer') from both onClick and Enter/Space, always calling e.stopPropagation() first. Colour map: queued and success var(--muted-foreground), in_progress var(--info), failure var(--destructive) — emerald is deliberately not used, per the style guide's one-colored-signal-per-row rule. Add the .projectCiChip class next to .featureCount (command-deck.module.css line 280) using var(--font-mono), 11px, font-weight 400, no background, no border, no border-radius: this is a text affordance, not a badge. No hardcoded hex, no slate-*, no font-bold/semibold, no rounded-full.

items.title: Given a store with no record for the project key, When ProjectCiChip renders, Then it produces no DOM output

Given a record with one in_progress suite and two completed successes, When ProjectCiChip renders, Then it shows the text 'CI 2/3' with data-ci-state="in_progress" and colour var(--info)

Given a multi-suite record, When the chip is clicked, Then window.open receives https://github.com/<repo>/commit/<headSha>/checks with '_blank'; given a single REST-sourced suite it receives that run's html_url
Given the rendered chip, When its class is inspected, Then the stylesheet rule uses var(--font-mono) with no border-radius, no background and no hardcoded hex colour
